classContent.en:
Students reviewed the two earlier homework options: a self-introduction and the printed glacier speech. The self-introduction focused on one main interest, with supporting details about when it began, what the speaker learned, and a future goal, followed by a return to the main point.

Students were encouraged to present what they remembered instead of relying on reading the full script. Stacey and Liam both demonstrated complete memorized presentations in their second attempts, correcting the earlier impression that the prepared speeches had not been shown. Tongtong also came up and spoke successfully after further encouragement. The lesson emphasized that students can begin, continue through small mistakes, and participate even when some vocabulary is unfamiliar.

The lesson began with warm-up activities and a review of homework. Students warmed up their voices, articulation and bodies, then focused on adding hand gestures and organizing ideas with “first,” “second” and “finally.” They practised an impromptu speech, trying to apply the feedback they had received.

Finally, students brainstormed and began crafting their next speech: “If I could have a dream robot.” They considered what their robot would do and what it would be capable of.

Preparation and attendance: Tongtong, Stacey and Liam had all memorized their previous speeches, which was a welcome surprise. This was Emily’s first class, so the previous homework requirement did not apply to her. Tianyou was absent, which is why no individual speaking feedback was recorded for this session.
classContent.zh:
学生回顾了之前的两种作业选择：自我介绍和打印的冰川演讲稿。自我介绍围绕一个主要兴趣展开，加入兴趣何时开始、学到了什么和未来目标等细节，并在结尾回到核心主题。

学生被鼓励讲出自己记住的内容，而不是依靠朗读完整稿件。Stacey和Liam在第二次尝试中都完整展示了背熟的演讲，修正了最初“还没有看到准备好的完整演讲”的印象。Tongtong也在进一步鼓励后上台，顺利进行了表达。课堂强调，即使有小错误或不熟悉的词，学生仍然可以开始、继续，并参与其中。

课堂开始时，我们进行了热身并回顾作业。学生进行了声音、吐字和身体热身，随后重点练习加入手势，并使用“first”“second”“finally”来组织想法。他们还练习了即兴演讲，尝试应用自己收到的反馈。

最后，学生围绕下一篇演讲“如果我能拥有一个梦想中的机器人”进行头脑风暴，并开始构思内容。他们思考了自己的机器人会做什么、具备哪些能力。

准备与出勤情况：Tongtong、Stacey 和 Liam 都已经背熟了之前的演讲，这让老师感到惊喜。这是 Emily 的第一节课，因此之前的作业要求不适用于她。Tianyou 本次缺席，所以没有记录本节课的个人演讲反馈。

homework.en:
If I could have a dream robot

Use the printed worksheet to develop your speech. Think about what your dream robot would do and what it would be capable of.

Try to complete the worksheet, memorize your speech, and be ready to present it in the next class.
homework.zh:
如果我能拥有一个梦想中的机器人

使用打印的学习单来准备演讲，思考你的梦想机器人会做什么、具备哪些能力。

请尝试完成学习单、记住自己的演讲，并准备在下节课展示。

classContent.en:
We began by reviewing the homework speeches. Students practised presenting with a voice loud enough for the audience to hear clearly.

We then introduced structures for answering impromptu questions, helping students organize an answer, explain their reasoning, and support their ideas with an example. The frameworks described were:

◆ PREP: Point, Reason, Example, Point.  
◆ OREO: Opinion, Reason, Example, Opinion.  
◆ Answer, Reason, Example, Message.  
◆ CREI: Claim, Reasoning, Example, Impact.  
◆ Connect, Answer, Reasoning, Example.

Students worked through four examples. They wrote out the first two answers to become comfortable with the structure and logic. They then practised answering without preparation, trying to follow PREP while speaking.
classContent.zh:
我们先复习了作业演讲。学生练习使用足够响亮的声音，让听众清楚听见。

接着，我们介绍了回答即兴问题的结构，帮助学生组织答案、解释理由，并用例子支持想法。课堂描述的框架包括：

◆ PREP：观点、理由、例子、重申观点。
◆ OREO：意见、理由、例子、重申意见。
◆ 回答、理由、例子、信息。
◆ CREI：主张、推理、例子、影响。
◆ 连接、回答、推理、例子。

学生完成了四个例子的练习。前两个先写出答案，以熟悉结构与逻辑；随后练习不做准备直接回答，尝试在讲话时使用 PREP。

homework.en:
Complete the last two written examples, using the structures introduced in class to organize the answers.

If possible, also practise the short dialogue between the bank robber and the security guard.
homework.zh:
完成最后两个书面例子，运用课堂介绍的结构组织答案。

如果可以，也请练习银行劫匪与保安之间的简短对话。

students.name: Stacey
students.en:
➜ Activity: “If I could have a dream robot” homework presentation.

➜ Preparation and delivery: Stacey remembered her homework and presented on stage without paper, using a loud voice. She met the requirements for the assignment and showed good preparation.

➜ Pacing: Her next step is to slow down slightly, giving the audience more time to follow and absorb her ideas.

➜ Content development: She could also speak a little longer by expanding an existing point—for example, explaining how one of her robot’s abilities would work or describing a situation in which it would help.

➜ Suggested practice: Keep the strong voice and independent delivery, add one specific detail, and rehearse at a slightly slower pace.
students.zh:
➜【活动】：“如果我能拥有一个梦想机器人”作业展示。

➜【准备与表达】：Stacey 记住了作业内容，不看稿纸在台上展示，声音响亮。她达到了本次作业要求，体现了良好的准备。

➜【语速】：下一步是稍微放慢，让听众有更多时间跟上并吸收想法。

➜【内容展开】：还可以把已有的一个要点讲得更充分，使演讲稍长一些。例如解释机器人的某项能力如何运作，或描述它能帮忙的一种情境。

➜【建议练习】：保持响亮的声音和独立展示，增加一个具体细节，并以稍慢的速度排练。

students.name: Naru
students.en:
➜ Activity: Self-introduction in her first class.

➜ Voice, logic, and content: Naru made a strong start in three areas: she spoke with a loud voice, organized her ideas logically, and developed her content well. On her first attempt, she successfully used the self-introduction structure to put together a clear presentation.

➜ Audience connection: Her next challenge is to connect more directly with the other students. An opening that addresses them—such as “boys and girls”—can make listeners feel included. Playful greetings such as “ladies and germs” or “ladies and worms” were also suggested as ways to introduce humor when appropriate.

➜ Suggested practice: Try opening with a greeting followed by a rhetorical question related to her topic. Pause briefly and look at the audience before continuing, giving the opening time to catch their attention.
students.zh:
➜【活动】：第一次上课的自我介绍。

➜【声音、逻辑与内容】：Naru 在三个方面有良好的开端：声音响亮、想法有逻辑、内容展开得好。第一次尝试就成功运用了自我介绍结构，完成清楚的展示。

➜【听众连接】：下一步是更直接地与其他学生建立联系。用“boys and girls”这样的称呼开场，会让听众觉得自己被包括在内。课堂也建议在合适的时候使用“ladies and germs”或“ladies and worms”这样的趣味问候，增加幽默感。

➜【建议练习】：尝试先问候，再加入一个与主题相关的设问。短暂停顿，看向听众后再继续，让开场有时间吸引注意。

students.name: Emily
students.en:
➜ Activity: “If I could have a dream robot” homework presentation.

➜ Preparation and completeness: Emily memorized her speech and included all the required parts. She spoke for 56 seconds, which was an appropriate length for this assignment—she does not need to make it longer to meet the requirement.

➜ Voice and stage presence: Her voice was a little soft, and she appeared shy on stage. The next step is to speak more loudly so the audience can hear her prepared ideas clearly.

➜ Suggested practice: Rehearse as though speaking to someone at the back of the classroom. Begin with a clear, strong first sentence and maintain that volume throughout, building comfort through repeated practice.
students.zh:
➜【活动】：“如果我能拥有一个梦想机器人”作业展示。

➜【准备与完整性】：Emily 记住了演讲，并包含所有要求的部分。她讲了 56 秒，长度符合本次作业要求，不需要为了达标而讲得更长。

➜【声音与台风】：她声音稍轻，在台上显得有些害羞。下一步是提高音量，让听众清楚听到她准备好的想法。

➜【建议练习】：排练时想象自己在对教室最后一排的人说话。用清楚、有力的第一句开始，并全程保持音量，通过重复练习增加舒适感。

students.name: Liam
students.en:
➜ Reading: Liam read from the text and completed his reading. He showed strength in reading aloud with the book as support.

➜ Presentation evidence: This attempt demonstrated reading from the book; independent recall and delivery without the text have not yet been confirmed.
students.zh:
➜【朗读】：Liam 看着文字朗读，并完成了阅读。他展现了借助书本朗读的能力。

➜【展示依据】：这次展示体现的是看书朗读；目前尚未确认他能独立回忆内容或脱离文字完成展示。

students.name: Ethan C.
students.en:
➜ Reading and voice: Ethan C. read aloud from his paper with a loud voice and showed strength in reading English. This presentation demonstrated his reading ability with the script available.

➜ Suggested practice: Keep the strong voice, and practise looking up from the paper after a short phrase to connect with the audience.
students.zh:
➜【朗读与声音】：Ethan C. 看着稿纸朗读，声音响亮，展现了英语朗读能力。这次展示体现的是有稿件支持时的朗读表现。

➜【建议练习】：保持响亮的声音，读完一个短语后尝试抬头看听众，增加交流。

students.name: Tongtong
students.en:
➜ Activity: “If I could have a dream robot” homework presentation.

➜ Recall and preparation: Tongtong had difficulty recalling her speech. With some prompting, she was able to speak, though she relied heavily on following the teacher’s words. Whether she completed the homework remains unconfirmed.

➜ Confidence and independence: She appeared hesitant and needed support to continue. The next step is to become comfortable sharing a short part of the speech independently, without needing each sentence supplied.

➜ Suggested practice: Rehearse one or two sentences at a time, then put the script aside and explain the idea in her own words. Start with a short section she knows well and gradually build toward the full presentation.
students.zh:
➜【活动】：“如果我能拥有一个梦想机器人”作业展示。

➜【回忆与准备】：Tongtong 难以回忆起演讲内容。在老师提示后，她能够开口，但较多依赖跟着老师的话说。目前尚不能确认她是否完成了课前作业。

➜【自信与独立表达】：她显得有些犹豫，需要支持才能继续。下一步是逐渐适应独立说出一小段内容，不需要老师逐句提供提示。

➜【建议练习】：每次练习一两句话，然后把稿子放在一旁，用自己的话解释意思。从熟悉的小段开始，逐步练习完整展示。

students.name: Remy
students.en: ✓ Remy was the first speaker and came up confidently, appearing comfortable talking in front of everyone. He had plenty of content to share, and his later attempt had a strong, loud voice. His main focus is organizing his ideas so he covers each part of the practised structure: introducing his main interest, explaining when he started, describing what he learned, and sharing a future goal before returning to his main point. This will help him give specific details while keeping the speech focused, especially when working within a time limit. In his first attempt, he sometimes seemed short of breath, so slowing down and pausing between ideas will also help him relax and give listeners time to absorb his message. His gestures were generally clear, although one or two small hand-to-face movements drew attention away from his message. For rehearsal, he should work through the structure in order, pause at each transition, and develop an interesting experience with a concrete example.
students.zh: ✓ Remy 是第一位上台的学生，表现自信，在大家面前讲话比较自在。他有不少内容可以分享，后一次展示的声音也很有力量、足够响亮。目前的重点是组织好想法，完整覆盖练习中的结构：介绍主要兴趣、说明何时开始、讲述学到的内容、分享未来目标，最后回到核心主题。这样既能加入具体细节，又能保持内容集中，尤其有助于今后在规定时间内完成演讲。第一次尝试中，他有时显得换气不够从容，因此放慢速度、在想法之间停顿，可以帮助他放松，也给听众时间消化内容。他的手势总体清楚，不过有一两次小的手部触脸动作让注意力偏离了内容。排练时，可以按顺序走完整个结构，在每个过渡处停顿，并用一个具体例子展开有趣的经历。

students.name: Pinkie
students.en: ✓ Pinkie spoke for more than a minute in her first attempt. Her voice was a little soft and her gestures were subtle, so building confidence and projecting more clearly remain important goals. In her later structured speech, she gave one sentence for each part of the framework, showing that she could follow the sequence. However, that attempt lasted only 24 seconds, and the ideas needed more explanation. For example, after saying what she learned, she could explain how she learned it or why it mattered; when describing a future goal, she could explain why she wants to pursue it. For her next rehearsal, she should keep the structure and add a reason or specific detail after each main statement. Regular stage practice, maintaining enough volume for the back of the room, and adding a clear gesture to support a point will help her develop a fuller, more expressive delivery.
students.zh: ✓ Pinkie 第一次展示超过了一分钟。她的声音偏轻，手势也较含蓄，因此建立上台自信、把声音更清楚地传出去仍是重要目标。后面的结构化演讲中，她为框架的每一部分各说了一句话，说明她能够跟随顺序。不过，这次只有24秒，想法还需要进一步解释。例如，说完学到了什么，可以补充如何学会、为什么重要；谈到未来目标，可以解释为什么想去做。下次排练时，她可以保留原有结构，在每个主要陈述后补充一个理由或具体细节。持续的舞台练习、让后排也能听到的音量，以及配合要点的清楚手势，都能帮助她的表达更充实、更有表现力。

students.name: Elsa
students.en: ✓ Elsa spoke for approximately one and a half to two minutes in her first attempt, but much of her introduction centred on a sad story about her pet hamster. This became the strongest impression left with listeners, so we discussed whether it was what she wanted the audience to remember about her. Follow-up questions, including possible topics such as gymnastics, drawing, or art, encouraged her to choose a main interest and develop details that would give listeners a clearer picture of who she is. In her later speech about liking dogs, she spoke confidently, maintained a steady pace, and followed the structure well. One small language point is remembering the plural ending in “I like dogs,” particularly when preparing for competitions where grammatical accuracy matters. She should also finish by returning to her main idea. A closing sentence such as “That’s one thing about me: I love dogs” gives the speech a clear ending and reinforces what the audience should remember.
students.zh: ✓ Elsa 第一次讲了大约一分半到两分钟，但自我介绍很大一部分围绕宠物仓鼠的一段伤心故事展开。这成了听众最深的印象，因此我们讨论了：这是否是她最希望大家记住的个人特点？通过追问，以及体操、绘画或艺术等可能的话题建议，我们鼓励她选择一个主要兴趣，加入能帮助听众更了解她的细节。后来讲到喜欢狗时，她表达自信、节奏平稳，也很好地使用了结构。一个小的语言重点是说“I like dogs”时记得复数词尾，尤其在准备比赛时，语法准确性也会受到关注。结尾还要回到主旨，例如“That’s one thing about me: I love dogs”。这样的收尾让演讲结束得清楚，也再次强调希望听众记住的信息。

students.name: Charlotte
students.en: ✓ Charlotte initially introduced a few things about herself quickly, then stopped before expanding her ideas. Follow-up questions helped her move from saying she liked drawing and “scribbling” to describing a futuristic city she had drawn. She explained that she had copied a picture at her mother’s suggestion, giving us a concrete starting point for discussing her drawing practice rather than assuming she was interested in designing cities. In her later attempt, she appeared more nervous and seemed concerned about finding the “perfect” or “right” answer. She sometimes became stuck partway through an idea without finishing her thought. We worked through the speech two or three times to help her express herself more smoothly. Her priority is becoming comfortable giving a simple, complete answer in her own words. During practice, she should finish the thought before trying to improve the wording, then add a detail about what she drew, how she worked on it, or what she enjoyed or found difficult.
students.zh: ✓ Charlotte 一开始很快地介绍了几件关于自己的事，随后就停了下来，没有进一步展开。通过追问，她从“喜欢画画”和“涂画”，逐渐说到自己画过的一座未来城市。她解释这是按照妈妈建议临摹的图片，因此我们有了具体的绘画练习内容可以讨论，而不是直接认定她对设计城市感兴趣。后一次尝试中，她显得更紧张，似乎很在意找到“完美”或“正确”的答案。有时说到一半就卡住，没有完成想法。我们一起练习了两到三遍，帮助她表达得更顺畅。目前最重要的是，让她习惯用自己的话说出一个简单、完整的回答。练习时，先把意思讲完，再改进措辞，然后补充自己画了什么、怎么画、喜欢什么，或遇到了什么困难。

students.name: Jarvis
students.en: ✓ Jarvis appeared a little nervous at first, keeping a hand behind his back and swinging his leg while speaking. As he settled in, he became more willing to express himself and let his hands come down naturally. In his later attempt, he made clear progress: he stopped putting his hands behind his back, covered everything he wanted to say, and delivered his ideas in a logical order. This showed that he could apply the feedback while still concentrating on his message. His next focus is becoming more aware of smaller body movements, particularly in his legs and feet, that he may not notice while speaking. During rehearsal, he should pause between main points to check that his feet are steady and his hands are relaxed. More opportunities to speak on stage will help him build on the confidence, organization, and improved body control he demonstrated during the lesson.
students.zh: ✓ Jarvis 刚开始有些紧张，一只手放在背后，讲话时腿也有摆动。逐渐适应后，他更愿意表达，双手也自然放了下来。后一次尝试中，他有明确的进步：不再把手放在背后，讲完了自己想说的内容，并且组织得有逻辑。这说明他能够在关注信息的同时运用反馈。下一步是更加留意细小的身体动作，尤其是自己讲话时可能没有注意到的腿部和脚部动作。排练时，可以在主要观点之间停顿，检查双脚是否稳定、双手是否放松。更多上台机会会帮助他继续发展本节课已经表现出的自信、组织能力和身体控制。

classContent.en:
Students practised self-introductions, answered follow-up questions, and delivered a second attempt using a clear speech structure. We focused on developing specific details so the audience could learn more about each speaker’s interests and experiences.

The structure was: “One thing about me is...,” “I started when...,” “What I learned was...,” and “In the future, I want to...,” followed by a conclusion returning to the main idea. We discussed how repeating the main point at the end helps listeners remember it.

At this stage, students are learning to feel comfortable speaking more and expanding their answers. As their confidence develops, they will also need to select and organize their content within a time limit. Individual delivery work included voice projection, pacing, pauses, gestures, and awareness of hands and feet on stage. As students become comfortable, they may be able to speak for three, five, or even ten minutes. For competitions and other timed presentations, they will then need to select what to keep and guide the speech toward its main point: first learning to say more, then learning to say it within a limit.
classContent.zh:
学生练习了自我介绍、回答追问，并按照清楚的演讲结构完成第二次尝试。我们重点练习加入具体细节，让听众更了解每位学生的兴趣和经历。

使用的结构是：“One thing about me is…”“I started when…”“What I learned was…”“In the future, I want to…”，最后用结尾回到核心主题。我们也讨论了，为什么在结尾重复重点能帮助听众记住内容。

现阶段，学生正在学习更自在地多说一些，把回答展开。随着自信增加，之后也需要学会在时间限制内选择和组织内容。个人表达指导包括声音投射、语速、停顿、手势，以及上台时对手脚动作的觉察。越来越自在后，学生可能能够讲三分钟、五分钟，甚至十分钟。但比赛和其他限时展示要求他们选择保留哪些内容，并让演讲始终围绕重点：先学会说得更多，再学会在规定时间内表达。

homework.en:
Write and rehearse your self-introduction

Introduce your name and one thing about yourself. Develop three supporting parts: when you started, what you learned, and what you would like to do in the future.

If possible, aim to write at least around 200 words. Use the writing process to organize your thoughts, logic and structure, rather than simply putting words on paper.

Practise and memorize the speech so you can deliver it in the next class. Aim for two minutes; one minute and thirty seconds is also acceptable.

Make sure you complete the task. If possible, send a video showing your completed speech.
homework.zh:
写作与排练：自我介绍

介绍自己的名字和一个关于自己的特点或兴趣，再展开三个支撑部分：你是什么时候开始的、从中学到了什么，以及未来想做什么。

如果可以，尽量写到至少约200个英文单词。写作不只是把内容写下来，也是整理想法、逻辑和结构的过程。

练习并记住演讲稿，准备在下节课展示。目标时长是两分钟；一分三十秒也可以接受。

请务必完成这项任务。如果可以，请发送一段视频，展示自己完成后的演讲。

classContent.en:
We began with voice and body warm-ups, followed by articulation practice. Students then reviewed and presented their self-introductions, with Jarvis speaking first. Feedback focused on controlling distracting hand movements, remembering prepared material, and connecting ideas logically so the audience could follow.

We then explored food waste in school cafeterias: the current problem, possible solutions, what some other schools are doing, and what students could choose to do themselves to reduce waste.

Students used a small amount of supplied evidence and information to develop their own opinions. They practised organizing and explaining their points with transitions such as “First,” “Second,” and “Finally.” The lesson included writing and presenting their topic-based speeches, with feedback on logic, detail, pronunciation, pauses, and delivery.

Completing homework at home is only part of the task. Students also need to prepare so they can present it in class, remembering what they intend to say or at least knowing their main ideas and their order. Written preparation helps students develop structure, logic, and specific details. Speaking practice helps them become comfortable communicating those ideas aloud. The aim is familiarity with the content, rather than reproducing every sentence perfectly. Students can use their own words: there is no single correct wording when sharing their own ideas.
classContent.zh:
我们先进行了声音和身体热身，随后练习吐字。学生接着复习并展示自我介绍，Jarvis 是第一位发言者。反馈重点包括控制分散注意力的手部动作、熟悉准备好的内容，以及让想法之间的逻辑联系更清楚，帮助听众跟上。

之后，我们探讨了学校食堂的食物浪费：目前的问题、可能的解决办法、其他一些学校正在采取的做法，以及学生自己可以选择怎样行动来减少浪费。

学生结合少量提供的证据和信息，发展自己的观点。他们练习用“First”“Second”“Finally”等过渡词组织并解释要点。课堂包括围绕这一主题写稿和展示，并针对逻辑、细节、发音、停顿及表达方式接受反馈。

在家完成作业只是任务的一部分。学生还需要做好准备，能够在课堂上展示，记得自己想说什么，或至少清楚主要想法及其顺序。书面准备有助于发展结构、逻辑和具体细节，开口练习则帮助学生更自在地传达这些想法。目标是熟悉内容，而不是逐字复述。分享自己的想法时，可以使用自己的语言，并不存在唯一正确的措辞。

homework.en:
Write out the food-waste speech and practise it aloud at home, ready to present next class. Organize the information and personal opinions clearly, use transitions, and explain the proposed actions for reducing waste.

Jarvis and Owen particularly need to complete the written work: the teacher felt they had not written their speeches during the activity. Elsa and Pinkie did not complete the previous homework, so completing this assignment was specifically emphasized. Their later writing and presentation efforts in class remain part of their positive progress.
homework.zh:
写出关于食物浪费的演讲稿，并在家大声练习，准备下节课展示。清楚组织信息和个人观点，使用过渡词，并解释建议采取哪些行动来减少浪费。

Jarvis 和 Owen 尤其需要完成书面内容：老师觉得他们在活动中没有写出演讲稿。Elsa 和 Pinkie 没有完成上一次作业，因此本次特别强调务必完成。他们后来在课堂中的写作和展示努力，也仍然是值得肯定的进步。

students.name: Pinkie
students.en:
✓ 𝑶𝒓𝒈𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒛𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒅𝒆𝒍𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚:
Pinkie had not completed the homework before class. However, she quickly organized her ideas and delivered an initial speech lasting approximately one to one and a half minutes—a positive attempt with limited preparation time.

✓ 𝑴𝒐𝒕𝒊𝒗𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒊𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆:
Later, Pinkie wanted to use her break time to finish writing what she planned to say. This showed motivation and a positive attitude toward preparing her work. She also came up and presented her organized ideas with good delivery.

➜ 𝑯𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒌 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Her effort during class was encouraging. The next step is to bring that same preparation to her homework before class. Speaking improves through both learning structures and practising delivery; completing the written preparation gives her time to strengthen the logic and connections between ideas.

➜ 𝑵𝒆𝒙𝒕 𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒑:
Prepare her ideas in writing and rehearse aloud before the next presentation, checking that each point connects clearly to the next.
students.zh:
✓【组织与表达】：
Pinkie 课前没有完成作业。不过，她很快整理了自己的想法，第一次演讲持续约一至一分半钟。在准备时间有限的情况下，这是一次积极的尝试。

✓【动机与态度】：
后来，Pinkie 想利用休息时间把准备说的内容写完。这体现了她准备作品的积极性和良好态度。她也上台展示了组织好的想法，表达表现不错。

➜【作业与练习】：
她在课堂中的努力值得鼓励。下一步是把这份准备态度延伸到课前作业。演讲进步既需要学习结构，也需要练习表达；完成书面准备，能让她有时间加强逻辑以及想法之间的联系。

➜【下一步】：
下次展示前，先写好想法，再大声排练，检查每个要点是否清楚地连接到下一个。

students.name: Owen
students.en:
✓ 𝑹𝒆𝒔𝒑𝒐𝒏𝒔𝒆 𝒕𝒐 𝒇𝒆𝒆𝒅𝒃𝒂𝒄𝒌:
At the beginning, Owen was using his fingers to play with a string while speaking. After a reminder, he stopped, showing that he could respond to feedback during his presentation. He should continue watching what his hands are doing so small movements do not distract from his message.

✓ 𝑽𝒐𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒍𝒐𝒈𝒊𝒄:
Owen spoke with a strong, loud voice. He explained that he likes food and would like to become a chef in the future. These ideas connected logically: his current interest led naturally into his future goal, making the speech easy to follow.

✓ 𝑶𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒂𝒍𝒍:
Owen missed the first class, but he was able to present and communicate the ideas he wanted to share. This was a good start.

➜ 𝑵𝒆𝒙𝒕 𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒑:
Speak for a little longer by developing the existing ideas. He could describe a food he enjoys and explain why he wants to become a chef, while keeping his hands relaxed and controlled.

✓ 𝑶𝒓𝒈𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒛𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Owen was able to organize his ideas quite well when speaking. However, he had not written down most of the content he presented.

➜ 𝑾𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒏 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒓𝒆𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍:
The concern is whether he will retain and build on those ideas after this attempt. Writing down the main points would give him something to revisit, rehearse, and improve, rather than relying on what he remembers from speaking once. His ability to organize ideas aloud is useful; the next step is to record enough of that thinking to support continued practice.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Write a short outline of his main ideas, then use it to rehearse and check whether he can explain them again.
students.zh:
✓【回应反馈】：
Owen 一开始讲话时用手指玩绳子。提醒后，他停止了这个动作，说明他能够在展示过程中回应反馈。今后仍应留意双手，避免小动作让听众分心。

✓【声音与逻辑】：
Owen 声音有力、响亮。他介绍自己喜欢食物，将来想成为厨师。两个想法之间有自然的逻辑联系：目前的兴趣引向未来目标，让听众容易理解。

✓【整体表现】：
Owen 错过了第一节课，但仍能够完成展示，表达自己想分享的内容。这是一个好的开始。

➜【下一步】：
在已有想法上继续展开，让演讲稍长一些。例如，可以介绍一种喜欢的食物，并解释为什么想成为厨师，同时保持双手放松、动作受控。

✓【组织能力】：
Owen 口头表达时能够较好地组织想法，但他没有写下展示中的大部分内容。

➜【书面准备与记忆】：
关注点在于，他能否在这次尝试后保留这些想法，并继续发展。写下主要要点，可以给他留下能够复习、排练和改进的材料，而不只是依靠说过一次之后的记忆。他能够口头组织内容是有用的基础；下一步是记录足够的思路，支持持续练习。

➜【建议练习】：
为主要想法写一个简短提纲，再用它排练，检查自己能否再次把内容解释清楚。

students.name: Jarvis
students.en:
➜ 𝑩𝒐𝒅𝒚 𝒍𝒂𝒏𝒈𝒖𝒂𝒈𝒆:
Jarvis showed some nervous hand movements while speaking. He needs to become more aware of these movements and control them so they do not draw attention away from his message. A useful rehearsal focus is to let his hands rest naturally between purposeful gestures.

➜ 𝑷𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒓𝒆𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍:
Jarvis did not appear to remember his prepared homework clearly. This does not establish whether he completed it at home, but it shows why preparation needs to include speaking practice. The goal is to arrive ready to share the material with the class, with enough familiarity to remember what he wants to say.

➜ 𝑳𝒐𝒈𝒊𝒄 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒐𝒓𝒈𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒛𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
His ideas moved through “chocolate, chocolate, vanilla, farmer, robot,” and the connections were difficult to follow. The relationship between these ideas was not clear to the listener. A useful practice would be to explain how each point connects to the next before rehearsing the full speech.
students.zh:
➜【肢体语言】：
Jarvis 讲话时出现了一些紧张的手部动作。他需要更加留意双手，并控制这些动作，避免分散听众对内容的注意力。排练时，可以练习在有目的的手势之间，让双手自然放松。

➜【准备与回忆】：
Jarvis 似乎没有清楚记住准备的作业。这并不能证明他在家没有完成，但说明准备过程中需要加入开口练习。目标是带着足够熟悉的内容来到课堂，能够记得自己想说什么，并向大家展示。

➜【逻辑与组织】：
他的想法依次涉及“chocolate, chocolate, vanilla, farmer, robot”，这些内容之间的联系不够清楚，听众较难跟上。在排练整篇演讲之前，可以先练习解释每个要点如何连接到下一个。

students.name: Remi
students.en:
✓ 𝑷𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒐𝒓𝒈𝒂𝒏𝒊𝒛𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Remi came with a written document and had put his content together before presenting. His preparation was clear: his speech sounded more logical and structured, with much more specific detail. Having his ideas organized on paper helped him explain them in a clearer sequence and gave listeners more information to follow.

➜ 𝑭𝒂𝒎𝒊𝒍𝒊𝒂𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒇𝒊𝒅𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆:
The next step is to become familiar enough with some of the content to look up and speak more freely. This does not mean memorizing every sentence exactly. There is no single “right” wording for sharing his own ideas, and he does not need to worry about reproducing the paper perfectly.

➜ 𝑵𝒆𝒙𝒕 𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒑:
He could practise one short section at a time: read it, look up, and explain the idea in his own words. The aim is to feel comfortable coming up to speak, enjoy sharing, and have fun.
students.zh:
✓【准备与组织】：
Remi 带来了书面材料，并在展示前整理好了内容。他的准备体现在表达中：演讲听起来更有逻辑、结构更清楚，也包含更多具体细节。提前在纸上组织想法，帮助他按照更清楚的顺序解释，让听众获得更多信息。

➜【熟悉程度与自信】：
下一步是进一步熟悉部分内容，让自己可以抬头、更自由地表达。这并不意味着逐字背诵。分享自己的想法没有唯一“正确”的措辞，也不必担心能否完美复述纸上的每一句话。

➜【下一步】：
可以一次练习一小段：先阅读，再抬头，用自己的话解释。目标是自在地上台、享受分享，并从讲话中获得乐趣。

students.name: Elsa
students.en:
✓ 𝑫𝒆𝒕𝒂𝒊𝒍 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒅𝒆𝒍𝒊𝒗𝒆𝒓𝒚:
She shared plenty of detail and was able to express her ideas. Her speech lasted approximately one minute and thirty seconds—a good length for this attempt.

➜ 𝑯𝒐𝒎𝒆𝒘𝒐𝒓𝒌:
She had not completed the homework. Although she was able to speak at length in class, completing the preparation remains important for developing her ideas and rehearsing her delivery.

➜ 𝑪𝒍𝒆𝒂𝒓 𝒆𝒏𝒅𝒊𝒏𝒈:
At the end of her speech, she needed to say “Thank you” to signal that she had finished. Without a clear ending, the silence left the audience unsure whether she was pausing or had completed her presentation.

➜ 𝑵𝒆𝒙𝒕 𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒑:
Practise the final sentence followed by “Thank you,” so the presentation ends clearly and confidently.

✓ 𝑾𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒏 𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒇𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒕:
Elsa gave a good presentation overall. Although she had not completed the homework before class, she had now worked through writing out her speech and attempted to deliver it using her script. This later effort is worth recognizing alongside the earlier homework concern.

➜ 𝑷𝒂𝒄𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒇𝒍𝒐𝒘:
Some pauses sounded mechanical or awkward, interrupting the natural flow. You suggested that she may still be getting used to reading aloud or delivering a longer speech; this remains a possible explanation rather than a confirmed cause.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Practise short sections aloud, keeping connected words together and pausing between complete ideas. Becoming more familiar with the script could help her delivery sound more natural.
students.zh:
✓【细节与表达】：
她分享了丰富的细节，能够表达自己的想法。演讲持续约一分三十秒，对这次尝试来说，时长不错。

➜【作业】：
她没有完成作业。虽然能够在课堂上持续表达，提前准备仍然有助于发展想法和排练。

➜【清楚收尾】：
演讲结束时，她需要说“Thank you”，让听众知道已经讲完。如果没有明确结束语，停下来的安静会让听众不确定她是在思考，还是已经完成展示。

➜【下一步】：
把最后一句与“Thank you”连起来练习，让演讲清楚、自信地结束。

✓【书面准备与努力】：
Elsa 后来的展示整体不错。虽然课前没有完成作业，但她已经认真写出了演讲内容，并尝试使用自己的稿子展示。这份后来的努力需要与之前的作业问题一起记录和肯定。

➜【节奏与流畅度】：
有些停顿显得机械或不自然，打断了表达的流畅度。老师提出，她可能还不太习惯朗读或展示较长的演讲；这只是可能的解释，并不是确定原因。

➜【建议练习】：
分小段大声练习，把意思相连的词语连贯说完，在完整想法之间停顿。更加熟悉稿子，可以帮助表达听起来更自然。

students.name: Richard
students.en: ✓ Richard was a little more timid than usual today and remained shy while speaking, but he was still willing to participate and come up for a second attempt. That willingness matters, and it is okay for him to need more time to settle into speaking in front of the group. The focus is helping him feel comfortable sharing his ideas without worrying about getting every sentence right. For his self-introduction, he can prepare a few simple points in his own words and rehearse them aloud, beginning with a steady opening sentence. Becoming familiar with what he wants to say should help him feel more settled when he presents again.
students.zh: ✓ Richard 今天比平时更拘谨，讲话时仍有些害羞，但他愿意参与，也愿意第二次上台尝试。这份意愿很重要，他可以有更多时间去适应在全班面前表达。现在的重点是帮助他自在地分享想法，不必担心每句话都要完全正确。准备自我介绍时，可以先用自己的话写下几个简单要点，再从一句平稳的开场开始，大声排练。对自己要说的内容更加熟悉，会帮助他下次展示时更加安定。

students.name: Molly
students.en: ✓ Molly was willing to come up and speak, even though this was something new for her and she appeared a little shy. She needed more support with finding the language to express her ideas, which sometimes made her delivery hesitant. She also relied on her paper while speaking. For now, we want to help her build a short introduction using words and sentences she understands and feels comfortable saying. During practice, she can work through one idea at a time, then look up and say it before checking her notes again. This will help her gradually become less dependent on reading while giving her the support she needs to express herself. Her willingness to participate is a good starting point to build on.
students.zh: ✓ 这对Molly来说是新的尝试，虽然有些害羞，她仍愿意上台发言。她在寻找合适的语言表达想法时需要更多支持，有时因此显得犹豫，讲话时也较依赖稿纸。目前希望帮助她用自己理解、也能自然说出的词句，建立一段简短的自我介绍。练习时，可以一次处理一个想法，先抬头说出来，再查看笔记。这样既能逐渐减少对朗读的依赖，也能保留她表达所需要的支持。她愿意参与，是可以继续发展的良好起点。

students.name: Angela
students.en: ✓ Angela spoke confidently and was willing to push herself to participate. This is a useful strength, and we want her to keep that enthusiasm while developing more consistent classroom habits. At times, she continued talking while others were speaking and left her seat for unrelated activities, which interrupted the group’s focus. She is working on recognizing when it is time to contribute and when it is time to listen. A gentle reminder at home about taking turns, giving classmates time to finish, and staying with the activity would support this. Her confidence gives her plenty to contribute; learning to manage that energy will help her participate more positively throughout the lesson.
students.zh: ✓ Angela 表达自信，也愿意主动挑战自己、参与发言。这是很好的基础，我们希望她保留这份热情，同时建立更稳定的课堂习惯。有时她在别人讲话时继续说话，或离开座位做与活动无关的事情，打断了全班的专注。她正在学习分辨什么时候适合表达、什么时候需要倾听。家长可以在家温和提醒她轮流发言、让同学把话说完，并跟随当前活动。她的自信让她有很多内容可以贡献；学会管理这份能量，将帮助她在整节课中更积极、合适地参与。

students.name: Juliana
students.en: ✓ Juliana showed a good level of confidence while speaking, particularly for her young age. Her command of English helped her express herself with a steady delivery, and she handled the speaking opportunities well overall. The next step is to help her use that language foundation to develop more of her own content. For her self-introduction, she can choose something she wants classmates to know about her and explain it with a reason or example. Writing and rehearsing those ideas herself will help her become more independent in preparing a speech, while building on the confidence she already showed in class.
students.zh: ✓ Juliana 年纪较小，但讲话时展现了不错的自信。她较好的英语掌握程度帮助她稳定地表达，整体也很好地把握了发言机会。下一步可以在这个语言基础上，发展更多自己的内容。准备自我介绍时，她可以选择一件想让同学了解的事，再用一个理由或例子解释。自己写出并排练这些想法，会帮助她更独立地准备演讲，同时继续发展课堂上已经表现出的自信。

students.name: Kiana
students.en: ✓ Kiana was confident on stage, although her overall presence was slightly less strong than during summer camp. Her delivery suggested that she was still getting back into the rhythm of presenting after some time away from stage practice. Regular opportunities to prepare and speak will help her regain that familiar ease. For the next class, she should write her self-introduction in her own words and rehearse it aloud while standing, gradually looking at her paper less often. This will help her become comfortable with both the content and the delivery, so she can give more attention to the audience when speaking.
students.zh: ✓ Kiana 在台上有自信，不过整体台风比夏令营时稍弱一些。她的表现让人感觉，她正在重新找回一段时间没有上台后的表达节奏。规律地准备和展示，可以帮助她恢复熟悉的从容感。下节课前，她可以用自己的语言写好自我介绍，站着大声排练，并逐渐减少看稿。这样能让她同时熟悉内容和表达方式，上台后把更多注意力放在听众身上。

classContent.en:
Today we worked on self-introductions, voice and body-language warm-ups, and an introduction to impromptu speech structure. During the superpower impromptu activity, students found it difficult to develop and express their own answers. Some were hesitant to share, so I provided speaking content to help them participate and practise the structure.

This does not mean they lack the ability to create their own speeches. They need more time and guided practice to develop their ideas and become comfortable expressing them. We will gradually reduce their reliance on paper, while continuing to use notes when needed. The priority is making sure they can form and communicate their own thoughts before expecting them to speak entirely without support.
classContent.zh:
今天练习了自我介绍、声音与肢体语言热身，并初步学习即兴演讲结构。在超能力即兴活动中，学生觉得发展并表达自己的答案有些困难。有些学生不太敢主动分享，因此老师提供了表达内容，帮助他们先参与并练习结构。

这不代表他们没有能力创作自己的演讲。他们需要更多时间和引导，去发展想法，并逐渐自在地表达。我们会慢慢减少对稿纸的依赖，同时在有需要时保留笔记支持。比起立即要求完全脱稿，更重要的是先确认学生能够形成并传达自己的思考。

homework.en: Students should write their own self-introduction and prepare to deliver it next class. Ideally, they should practise enough to present from memory without looking at the paper. Parents can help by asking questions, listening, and encouraging rehearsal, while allowing the ideas and wording to remain the student’s own. A simple introduction they have written and understand is a useful starting point.
homework.zh: 学生需要自己写一篇自我介绍，并准备下节课展示。理想情况下，通过练习可以不看稿、凭记忆表达。家长可以用提问、倾听和鼓励排练的方式提供帮助，同时让内容和措辞保持为学生自己的想法。由学生自己写出、自己理解的简单介绍，就是有价值的起点。
