students.name: Ray
students.en:
✓ Ray spoke for one minute, which was a good starting point for an unguided self-introduction. He moved his legs frequently while presenting, so one focus is becoming more aware of his body and keeping his feet steady. His introduction gave listeners limited new information about him, leaving room to develop his ideas further. He can choose one interest or experience and explain how he started, what he enjoys about it, or something specific he has done. Rehearsing with both feet planted comfortably will help him reduce distracting movement while giving more attention to his message.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: He could develop a personal detail with “I started when… One thing I remember is…”. A concrete moment helps listeners picture the experience instead of hearing only a list of interests. Practising that short section with steady feet can connect content development and body awareness in one manageable task.
students.zh:
✓ Ray 讲了一分钟，作为没有提示的自我介绍，这是一个不错的起点。展示时他的腿部动作较多，因此一个重点是增强身体觉察，让双脚保持稳定。介绍中让听众新了解到的信息还比较有限，内容可以进一步展开。他可以选择一个兴趣或经历，说明如何开始、喜欢什么，或具体做过的一件事。排练时双脚自然站稳，有助于减少分散注意力的动作，把更多注意力放在要传达的信息上。

➜ 意义与练习方法：他可以用“I started when… One thing I remember is…”来展开个人细节。具体的片段能让听众想象这段经历，而不只是听到兴趣清单。双脚站稳练习这一小段，可以把内容展开和身体觉察结合成一个容易完成的任务。

students.name: Harper
students.en: ✓ Harper spoke at a steady pace and used an audible voice, making her introduction easy to follow. She shared information about herself and appeared happy while speaking, bringing some enthusiasm to her delivery. Her introduction lasted 43 seconds, so she could expand it by adding a specific detail or example to one of her points. Her main delivery adjustment is slightly stronger voice projection. She was already loud enough to hear, but a little more volume would help her reach the whole room. She should keep her steady pace and cheerful expression while practising as though she is addressing someone at the back of the classroom.
students.zh: ✓ Harper 语速平稳，声音能让人听见，因此自我介绍比较容易跟上。她分享了自己的信息，讲话时显得开心，带有一定热情。介绍持续了43秒，可以在其中一个要点后补充具体细节或例子，让内容更充实。表达方面最主要的调整是再加强一点声音投射。她已经能被听见，但稍微提高音量，会更好地覆盖整个教室。练习时可以想象自己在对教室后排的人讲话，同时保持平稳的节奏和愉快的表情。

students.name: Evan
students.en: ✓ Evan initially began delivering a speech, then recognized that the task was a self-introduction and adjusted his content. He remembered to clap as part of the distraction challenge, which showed attention to the additional instruction while speaking. After a while, he became unsure what else to say. His next focus is learning how to expand an idea rather than stopping after the first statement. For example, he can describe an interest or experience, then explain what happened, why he enjoyed it, or how he felt. Practising this process will give him a clearer direction when he feels he has run out of content and help listeners learn more about him.
students.zh: ✓ Evan 起初像是在发表另一篇演讲，随后意识到任务是自我介绍，并调整了内容。他记得按分心挑战的要求拍手，说明讲话时也在留意额外指令。讲了一会儿后，他开始不确定还能补充什么。下一步是学习如何展开一个想法，而不是说完第一句话就停下。例如，介绍一个兴趣或经历后，可以说明发生了什么、为什么喜欢，或当时有什么感受。练习这个过程，可以让他在觉得“没内容可说”时找到继续的方向，也让听众更了解他。

students.name: Mikaela
students.en: ✓ Mikaela showed a little more confidence and appeared to have maintained her previous progress. Her voice was audible, and she brought some enthusiasm to her introduction, although slightly stronger projection would help. After about 30–40 seconds, her speech tapered off, seemingly because she was unsure what else to add. Her main focus is finishing clearly, even when her speech is short. A closing such as “That’s me!” or “Thank you!” tells the audience she has finished and helps her maintain confidence through the ending. During rehearsal, she should practise her last main point together with a closing sentence, keeping her voice strong through the final word.
students.zh: ✓ Mikaela 表现得更自信一些，也保持了之前的进步。她的声音能被听见，自我介绍中也有一些热情，不过声音投射还可以再强一点。大约30–40秒后，她的表达逐渐收弱，似乎是不确定还能补充什么。目前最重要的是，即使演讲较短，也要清楚地结束。“That’s me!”或“Thank you!”这样的收尾，可以让听众知道她已经讲完，也帮助她把自信保持到最后。排练时，把最后一个主要信息与结束语连起来练习，并把声音保持到最后一个词。

students.name: Rhea
students.en:
✓ Rhea introduced herself as six years old and spoke quite fluently, although she appeared a little timid on stage. Her playful description of running “ten hours every day” brought some personality and energy to her introduction. Her main focus is making her voice stronger so that listeners can hear her clearly and stay engaged. She can practise addressing someone across the room with a clear, projected voice without shouting. She was able to keep her words flowing; the next step is helping her feel comfortable using enough volume to share those ideas with the whole audience.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: A useful check is whether the last word of each sentence reaches the listener as clearly as the first. She can practise one familiar sentence across the room, pause for a breath, and repeat it with the same clarity. This builds consistent projection while allowing her playful personality to remain part of the introduction.
students.zh:
✓ Rhea 介绍自己六岁，虽然在台上有些拘谨，表达却比较流畅。她用“每天跑十小时”这样带有玩笑性质的说法，展现了自己的个性和活力。目前的重点是让声音更有力量，让听众听清并保持关注。练习时，可以对房间另一边的人用清楚、有投射力的声音讲话，而不是喊叫。她已经能够连贯地说出想法，接下来要帮助她适应使用足够的音量，把这些内容分享给全场听众。

➜ 意义与练习方法：可以检查每句话最后一个词是否与第一个词一样清楚地传到听众那里。她可以面向房间另一端说一句熟悉的话，停顿换气后，再保持同样的清晰度重复。这能帮助她稳定投射声音，同时保留自我介绍中活泼的个性。

students.name: Wendy
students.en:
✓ Wendy had plenty to share, including a playful claim about running for “40 hours nonstop.” She spoke loudly and clearly. When she was unsure what to say next, she took time to think and then continued, which was a useful way to manage the moment. She did not include the clap from the distraction challenge, so that is something to remember when following additional speaking instructions. Overall, she gave a good performance. Her next focus is bringing more enthusiasm into her voice, such as emphasizing what she enjoys most, so her delivery attracts attention as well as communicating clearly.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: She can mark a meaningful word in each sentence and decide whether a pause, gesture, or change of tone best highlights it. Rehearsing the extra challenge cue alongside the speech can make it easier to remember both. The aim is purposeful expression that helps the audience recognize important ideas, rather than simply adding more volume.
students.zh:
✓ Wendy 有很多内容愿意分享，也用了“连续跑40小时”这样的玩笑表达。她的声音响亮、清楚。不知道接下来该说什么时，她会先想一想，再继续，这是处理临场停顿的有效方式。她没有加入分心挑战要求的拍手动作，因此今后还要留意额外的发言指令。整体表现不错。下一步是让声音更有热情，例如强调自己最喜欢的部分，让表达既清楚，也更能吸引听众。

➜ 意义与练习方法：她可以在每句话中标出一个有意义的词，再决定用停顿、手势还是语调变化来突出它。把额外的挑战提示与演讲一起练习，有助于兼顾两项要求。目标是有目的的表达，让听众辨认重要想法，而不只是增加音量。

students.name: Ethan
students.en: ✓ Ethan spoke fluently and at length, with very good pacing, pauses, and enthusiasm. He had plenty to share and was comfortable developing a longer introduction. His main focus is filtering his language and considering the impression he leaves with his audience. When describing strong feelings or opinions, he should choose respectful wording that accurately communicates his interest or passion. For example, he can describe being passionate about an interest or enjoying discussion, using language that fits what he actually means. He can also be more specific: rather than simply saying he plays games on his phone, he could name a game he enjoys and explain what interests him about it. Including other interests and experiences will give listeners a fuller picture of who he is. For rehearsal, he should review what each point tells the audience about him while keeping his energetic, well-paced delivery.
students.zh: ✓ Ethan 表达流畅，能够持续讲较长时间，语速、停顿和热情都很好。他有不少内容可以分享，也能自在地展开较长的自我介绍。目前的重点是筛选语言，考虑自己给听众留下的印象。描述强烈情绪或观点时，应选择尊重他人、又能准确表达兴趣与热情的措辞。例如，可以表达自己对某个兴趣很投入、喜欢讨论，同时确保这些说法符合真实意思。内容也可以更具体：与其只说喜欢在手机上玩游戏，不如说出喜欢的游戏，并解释什么地方吸引自己。同时加入其他兴趣和经历，可以让听众更全面地了解他。排练时，逐点检查每个信息让听众了解到什么，并保持他已有的活力和良好节奏。

classContent.en:
We began with voice, articulation, and body warm-ups. Students then gave a brief self-introduction without hints or guidance, allowing us to see how independently they could organize and express their ideas. Returning students had an additional distraction challenge: clapping or saying “hooray” at the end of a sentence while keeping track of what they wanted to say.

We then explored different occupations and practised the related speeches. Students received feedback and worked on applying it during their second or third attempts. Together, we also created a story for emotional-expression practice, switching between happy, scrunched-up, sad, and shocked expressions. We repeated these exercises and practised stronger voice projection.
classContent.zh:
我们先进行了声音、吐字和身体热身。随后，学生在没有提示或指导的情况下做简短自我介绍，以观察他们独立组织、表达想法的情况。老生还有一个额外的分心挑战：在句末拍手或说“hooray”，同时继续记住自己想说的内容。

之后，我们探讨不同职业，并练习相关演讲。学生接受反馈后，在第二次或第三次尝试中练习运用。全班还共同创作了一个故事，用来练习情绪表达，在开心、皱起脸、伤心和惊讶之间切换。我们重复了这些练习，也加强了声音投射训练。

homework.en: Students should practise and memorize the speech for their chosen occupation, ready to present it next class. Sending a practice video is encouraged so we can see their preparation and delivery.
homework.zh: 学生需要练习并记住自己选择的职业演讲，准备下节课展示。鼓励发送练习视频，让老师看到准备情况和表达效果。

classContent.en:
We began by reviewing the homework speeches about occupations. Students practised presenting with a voice loud enough for the audience to hear clearly.

We then introduced structures for answering impromptu questions, helping students organize an answer, explain their reasoning, and support their ideas with an example. The frameworks described were:

◆ PREP: Point, Reason, Example, Point.  
◆ OREO: Opinion, Reason, Example, Opinion.  
◆ Answer, Reason, Example, Message.  
◆ CREI: Claim, Reasoning, Example, Impact.  
◆ Connect, Answer, Reasoning, Example.

Students worked through four examples. They wrote out the first two answers to become comfortable with the structure and logic. They then practised answering without preparation, trying to follow PREP while speaking.
classContent.zh:
我们先复习了关于职业的作业演讲。学生练习使用足够响亮的声音，让听众清楚听见。

接着，我们介绍了回答即兴问题的结构，帮助学生组织答案、解释理由，并用例子支持想法。课堂描述的框架包括：

◆ PREP：观点、理由、例子、重申观点。
◆ OREO：意见、理由、例子、重申意见。
◆ 回答、理由、例子、信息。
◆ CREI：主张、推理、例子、影响。
◆ 连接、回答、推理、例子。

学生完成了四个例子的练习。前两个先写出答案，以熟悉结构与逻辑；随后练习不做准备直接回答，尝试在讲话时使用 PREP。

homework.en:
Complete the last two written examples, using the structures introduced in class to organize the answers.

If possible, also practise the short dialogue between the bank robber and the security guard.
homework.zh:
完成最后两个书面例子，运用课堂介绍的结构组织答案。

如果可以，也请练习银行劫匪与保安之间的简短对话。

students.name: Wendy
students.en:
✓ 𝑷𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒇𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒕:
Wendy completed three speaking attempts, giving her repeated opportunities to practise her delivery.

➜ 𝑽𝒐𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒋𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Her voice remained soft and small across the attempts. She needs to project more strongly so her words reach the audience clearly.

➜ 𝑨𝒖𝒅𝒊𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒕𝒂𝒄𝒕:
Wendy looked at her paper rather than at the audience. Becoming more familiar with her content would help her look up and share her ideas with listeners.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Hold the paper lower, glance at one short sentence, then look up and say it to someone across the room. Keep the voice strong through the final word before checking the paper again.
students.zh:
✓【练习与努力】：
Wendy 完成了三次发言尝试，获得了反复练习表达的机会。

➜【声音投射】：
几次尝试中，她的声音仍然偏轻、偏小。她需要加强声音投射，让听众清楚听到每句话。

➜【听众交流】：
Wendy 看着稿纸，没有看向听众。更加熟悉内容，可以帮助她抬头，把想法分享给面前的人。

➜【建议练习】：
把纸放低，看一眼短句，再抬头对房间另一端的人说出来。保持声音有力直到最后一个词，然后再查看稿纸。

students.name: Mikaela
students.en:
✓ 𝑬𝒇𝒇𝒐𝒓𝒕 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒓𝒆𝒑𝒆𝒂𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Mikaela came up for another attempt, making approximately three tries in total. She continued practising, although her voice remained soft in the final attempt.

➜ 𝑽𝒐𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒑𝒓𝒐𝒋𝒆𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Her voice was difficult to hear during the earlier attempts and was still small on the last try. The immediate focus is helping her produce a comfortably audible voice. There was not enough clearly heard content to assess her speech’s ideas or organization.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Begin with “Hello, my name is Mikaela,” addressed clearly to one listener. Practise making the whole sentence audible without shouting, then gradually increase the distance. Short, manageable attempts can give her a clear target for practising projection.

➜ Additional rehearsal option: Start with one short sentence addressed to someone at the back of the room, using a clear, supported voice without shouting. Once it is audible, practise maintaining that volume through the next sentence.
students.zh:
✓【努力与反复练习】：
Mikaela 再次上台尝试，总共约三次。她继续练习，不过最后一次声音仍然偏轻。

➜【声音投射】：
前几次尝试中，她的声音较难听清，最后一次仍然偏小。当前重点是帮助她用舒适、能够被听见的声音表达。由于听清的内容不足，目前无法评价演讲的想法或组织。

➜【建议练习】：
先面对一位听众清楚说出“Hello, my name is Mikaela”。练习不用喊叫也能让整句话被听见，再逐渐拉开距离。简短、容易完成的尝试，可以给她一个明确的声音练习目标。

➜【另一种排练方法】：
先用清楚、有支持的声音，向教室后排的人说一句短句，不需要喊叫。确认听得见后，再练习把同样的音量保持到下一句。

students.name: Evan
students.en:
✓ 𝑷𝒓𝒐𝒈𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒔 𝒂𝒄𝒓𝒐𝒔𝒔 𝒂𝒕𝒕𝒆𝒎𝒑𝒕𝒔:
Evan spoke softly during his first and second attempts. For his third attempt, lively music was added, and he spoke much more loudly. This was a clear improvement in volume.

➜ 𝑪𝒍𝒂𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒚 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒄𝒐𝒎𝒑𝒐𝒔𝒖𝒓𝒆:
During the louder attempt, Evan began giggling while speaking, which made parts of his message harder to understand. His next focus is maintaining that stronger voice while keeping his words clear and steady.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Practise one complete sentence at a strong, clear volume. If laughter interrupts, pause, take a breath, and repeat the sentence so the audience can understand every word.
students.zh:
✓【多次尝试中的进步】：
Evan 第一次和第二次讲话都比较轻。第三次加入了活泼的音乐，他的声音明显响亮了许多，音量有清楚的进步。

➜【清晰度与稳定表达】：
声音变大的这次尝试中，他边讲话边笑，导致部分内容不容易听懂。下一步是保持较强的声音，同时把词句说得清楚、稳定。

➜【建议练习】：
用有力、清楚的音量练习一个完整句子。如果笑声打断表达，可以停一下、换口气，再把句子说一遍，让听众听懂每个词。

students.name: Everleigh
students.en:
✓ 𝑽𝒐𝒊𝒄𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑬𝒙𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Everleigh spoke with a loud voice and showed a good level of English. Her vocabulary helped her express her ideas, giving her a useful foundation for participating in the class.

✓ 𝑺𝒑𝒆𝒆𝒄𝒉 𝒔𝒕𝒓𝒖𝒄𝒕𝒖𝒓𝒆:
She independently used “first” and “second” to organize her points, despite not having attended this class before. This showed an initial ability to put her ideas into a sequence that listeners could follow.

✓ 𝑪𝒍𝒂𝒔𝒔 𝒔𝒖𝒊𝒕𝒂𝒃𝒊𝒍𝒊𝒕𝒚:
Based on this trial, she appears ready to participate in the class. Her audible voice, vocabulary, and emerging structure provide a good starting point.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Build on “first” and “second” by adding a reason or example after each point.
students.zh:
✓【声音与表达】：
Everleigh 讲话声音响亮，展现了不错的英语水平。她的词汇能够支持她表达自己的想法，为参与课堂提供了有用的基础。

✓【演讲结构】：
虽然之前没有参加过这门课，她已经能够自主用“first”和“second”组织要点，初步展现了按顺序安排想法、帮助听众理解的能力。

✓【课程适合度】：
根据这次试听，她看来能够参与这门课。清楚可闻的声音、词汇以及初步结构意识，都是不错的起点。

➜【建议练习】：
在“first”和“second”的基础上，为每个要点补充一个理由或例子。

students.name: Zoey
students.en:
✓ Zoey spoke for one minute with a steady pace and a calm delivery. Her presentation was easy to listen to, and there were no other notable issues in this attempt. Her next step is to bring a little more energy into her voice while keeping the comfortable pacing she already demonstrated. For practice, she can choose one point she particularly wants the audience to remember and say it with slightly more emphasis and enthusiasm. This will help make her delivery more expressive while preserving the calm, clear style that worked well today.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: For example, she can say “The part I enjoy most is…” and experiment with emphasizing the important words. She can then ask a listener which idea stood out. This makes vocal energy purposeful: the aim is to highlight meaning, while keeping the steady pace that already makes her comfortable to listen to.
students.zh:
✓ Zoey 讲了一分钟，节奏平稳、表达从容，听起来很舒服。这次没有其他明显问题。下一步可以在保留现有舒适节奏的同时，让声音多一点能量。练习时，选择一个最希望听众记住的重点，用稍强的重音和热情说出来。这样能够增加表现力，同时保留今天有效的平静、清楚的表达风格。

➜ 意义与练习方法：例如，她可以说“The part I enjoy most is…”，尝试强调其中重要的词，再请听众说出印象最深的想法。这样，声音的能量就有了明确目的：突出意义，同时保留已经让听众感到舒服的稳定节奏。

students.name: Peter
students.en: ✓ Peter spoke with a loud, clear voice and plenty of energy. His pronunciation was clear in this attempt, so articulation is not the main concern. His focus is managing his excitement and keeping his body steady while speaking. Earlier, he jumped up and down and became more excited when the audience was noisy, which made it harder for him to stay focused on his message. For practice, he should keep both feet on the floor, deliver a complete thought, and pause before continuing. His strong voice and enthusiasm are useful strengths; greater control of his movements will help the audience give their attention to what he is saying.
students.zh: ✓ Peter 的声音响亮、清楚，也很有能量。这次的发音清晰，因此吐字并不是主要问题。目前更需要管理兴奋感，让身体在讲话时保持稳定。之前他有跳动的情况，听众较吵时也会更加兴奋，使他不容易专注于自己要说的内容。练习时，可以双脚站在地面，讲完一个完整的想法，再停顿后继续。他有力量的声音和热情都是优势；更好地控制动作，会帮助听众把注意力放在他的内容上。

students.name: Merlin
students.en: ✓ Merlin brought a powerful voice and plenty of energy to his speech, which drew the audience’s attention. His main delivery focus is slowing down and pausing between sentences, as his fast pace made parts of his message difficult to understand. Practising one sentence at a time, finishing each word clearly before continuing, will help him make better use of his strong voice. During class, he also repeatedly made noises while others were speaking, which interrupted their turns and distracted listeners. We are working on helping him direct his energy appropriately: raising his hand before contributing, keeping his materials quiet, and giving the speaker his attention. Gentle reinforcement at home would support these habits so he can participate enthusiastically while allowing classmates the same opportunity to be heard.
students.zh: ✓ Merlin 的声音很有力量，表达充满能量，能够吸引听众注意。目前的主要表达重点是放慢速度，并在句子之间停顿，因为较快的语速让部分内容不容易听懂。可以一次练习一句，把每个词清楚说完再继续，让有力量的声音发挥更好的作用。课堂中，他也多次在别人讲话时发出声音，打断了同学的发言，并分散听众注意力。我们正在帮助他把能量用在合适的地方：发言前举手、安静使用手中的材料，并把注意力给台上的同学。家长在家温和强化这些习惯，可以帮助他保持参与热情，同时让其他同学也有被听见的机会。

students.name: Oliver
students.en: ✓ Oliver used a very loud voice in his earlier attempt, and his turn lasted approximately two minutes and thirty seconds, including considerable time spent thinking between points, with hand movements and walking that distracted from his message. He still needs to become more aware of his hands and maintain a stronger voice consistently. When using notes, he should hold the paper with one hand, keep it low enough to see the audience, and look toward the people in front of him as he speaks. For practice, he can glance at one point, look up, and deliver the complete sentence clearly before checking his paper again. This will help him combine steadier movement, audience contact, and audible speech. During pauses, he can keep his hands relaxed by his sides or comfortably in front, using gestures when they support an idea. Preparing a few simple points will help him move from one to the next with a brief pause and steady posture.
students.zh: ✓ Oliver 较早的一次尝试声音很响亮，整轮约两分三十秒，其中包含了较多思考下一点的时间，手部动作和走动也让听众分心。他仍需要更留意自己的双手，并持续保持较强的声音。使用笔记时，可以单手拿纸，放低到能看见听众的位置，讲话时看向面前的人。练习时，先看一个要点，再抬头把完整句子清楚说出来，之后再看稿。这样能把更稳定的动作、与听众的眼神交流，以及清楚可闻的表达结合起来。停顿时，双手可以放松垂在身体两侧，或自然放在身前，在支持观点时再使用手势。提前准备几个简单要点，也能帮助他在短暂停顿、保持稳定站姿的情况下，顺利进入下一点。

students.name: Lucas
students.en: ✓ Lucas was able to express himself while the audience listened attentively. In his earlier attempt, he spoke for about two minutes, but his voice faded toward the end and there was no clear conclusion, leaving listeners unsure whether he had finished. When using his paper, he tends to hold it high with both hands, and his voice also tapers off as he reads. His main focus is maintaining an audible voice throughout the speech while managing his notes more comfortably. During practice, he should hold the paper lower with one hand, glance down when needed, and look up to deliver each sentence clearly. He should also rehearse his final point together with a short closing, keeping the same strong volume through the last word so the audience knows he has finished.
students.zh: ✓ Lucas 在同学认真倾听时，能够表达自己的想法。较早的一次尝试讲了约两分钟，但接近结尾时声音变弱，也没有清楚的收尾，让听众不确定他是否已经结束。使用稿纸时，他容易双手把纸举得较高，读着读着声音也逐渐变小。目前最重要的是在整段演讲中保持可听见的音量，并更自然地使用笔记。练习时，把纸放低，用一只手拿，需要时看一眼，再抬头清楚说出每句话。最后一个要点要与简短的结束语一起排练，让声音一直保持到最后一个词，使听众明确知道演讲已经结束。

students.name: Arthur
students.en: ✓ Arthur spoke with a loud voice and a big smile in his later attempt, bringing more expression to his delivery. In his first introduction, he said “I am Arthur” but struggled to add more, even with prompts, and spent time laughing rather than continuing. His next step is to prepare a few simple points about himself so he knows what to say after his name. He can practise sharing one thing he likes and explaining why, using a deliberate hand gesture to support the idea. This will help him bring more energy to his speech while keeping his hands under control. During class, he also needs to remember to raise his hand and wait for his turn, giving others the opportunity to speak.
students.zh: ✓ Arthur 在后一次尝试中声音响亮，脸上有大大的笑容，表达也更生动。第一次自我介绍时，他说了“I am Arthur”，但即使得到提示，也不太容易继续展开，有一段时间在笑，没有接着说。下一步是准备几个简单的个人要点，让他知道说完名字后还能说什么。可以练习介绍一件喜欢的事，并说明理由，再加一个有目的的手势来配合内容。这会帮助他增加表达能量，同时控制好双手。课堂中也要记得举手、等待轮到自己，让其他同学有发言机会。

classContent.en:
Students practised introductions and repeated speaking turns, applying feedback on voice, articulation, pace, hand control, and audience contact. When using paper, they worked on holding it lower in one hand, looking up, and delivering a complete sentence before checking the next point.

Our immediate delivery priority was a louder, clear voice that reaches the audience from the beginning to the end of each speech. Students also practised finishing with a clear closing, managing their movements while thinking, raising a hand before contributing, and listening quietly while classmates spoke.

This first lesson included both new students and students who had attended classes before. We used articulation, voice and body-language warm-ups, impromptu speaking practice, and self-introductions. Even for students who had introduced themselves before, the aim was to express themselves more clearly.

The self-introduction structure was: “My name is…”; “One thing about me is…”; when I started; what I have learned through this experience; and what I want to do in the future. Students then returned to the main idea with a sentence such as “That is why one thing about me is…”, followed by a clear conclusion.

The objectives differed according to each student’s public-speaking experience. For returning students, the lesson was an opportunity to see how their speaking had improved. For new students, the priority was to feel comfortable speaking on stage in front of everyone. Students who had attended summer camp were encouraged to demonstrate eye contact, a loud voice, a slightly longer speech, more vivid details and hand gestures. For new students, simply coming up to speak was a worthwhile first step.
classContent.zh:
学生练习了自我介绍和多轮发言，并运用有关声音、吐字、语速、手部控制和听众交流的反馈。使用稿纸时，练习单手把纸放低、抬头表达，并把一个完整句子说完后再查看下一个要点。

当前的主要表达目标是声音更响亮、清楚，从开头到结尾都能传到听众那里。学生也练习了明确收尾、在思考时管理身体动作、发言前举手，以及同学讲话时安静倾听。

这是本期的第一节课，班上既有新同学，也有之前上过课的学生。课堂包括吐字、声音和肢体表达热身、即兴表达练习，以及自我介绍。即使学生之前做过自我介绍，我们仍希望他们能把自己表达得更清楚。

自我介绍的结构是：“My name is…”；“One thing about me is…”；我什么时候开始；我从这段经历中学到了什么；以及未来想做什么。然后用“That is why one thing about me is…”这样的句子回到主要特点，并用明确的总结句收尾。

每位学生的目标根据公众演讲经验有所不同。对于老生，这节课帮助我们了解他们在表达上有哪些进步；对于新生，重点是逐渐适应站在舞台上，在大家面前讲话。参加过夏令营的学生，可以进一步展示眼神交流、响亮的声音、稍长的演讲、更生动的细节和手势。对于新同学，愿意上台开口就是值得肯定的第一步。

homework.en:
Write and practise your self-introduction

Write out your self-introduction: your name, one thing about yourself, when you started, what you have learned through the experience, and what you want to do in the future. Finish by returning to your main idea and adding a concluding sentence.

Practise the speech and, if possible, memorize it so you can deliver it in the next class.

For students who previously attended summer camp, focus on eye contact, a loud voice, a slightly longer speech with more vivid details, and hand gestures.

For new students, coming up to the stage and speaking in front of everyone is a good first goal. Expectations will reflect each student’s current stage in learning public speaking.
homework.zh:
写作与练习：自我介绍

写出自己的自我介绍：名字、一个关于自己的特点或兴趣、什么时候开始、从这段经历中学到了什么，以及未来想做什么。结尾回到主要特点，并用一句总结句收尾。

练习演讲，如果可以，请记住演讲稿，准备在下节课展示。

对于参加过夏令营的学生，重点关注眼神交流、响亮的声音、稍长一些且细节更生动的演讲，以及手势的运用。

对于新同学，愿意走上台，在大家面前开口讲话，就是一个很好的起点。要求会根据每位学生目前的公众演讲学习阶段有所不同。

classContent.en:
We began by reviewing the homework speeches. Students practised presenting with a voice loud enough for the audience to hear clearly.

We then introduced structures for answering impromptu questions, helping students organize an answer, explain their reasoning, and support their ideas with an example. The frameworks described were:

◆ PREP: Point, Reason, Example, Point.  
◆ OREO: Opinion, Reason, Example, Opinion.  
◆ Answer, Reason, Example, Message.  
◆ CREI: Claim, Reasoning, Example, Impact.  
◆ Connect, Answer, Reasoning, Example.

Students worked through four examples. They wrote out the first two answers to become comfortable with the structure and logic. They then practised answering without preparation, trying to follow PREP while speaking.
classContent.zh:
我们先复习了作业演讲。学生练习使用足够响亮的声音，让听众清楚听见。

接着，我们介绍了回答即兴问题的结构，帮助学生组织答案、解释理由，并用例子支持想法。课堂描述的框架包括：

◆ PREP：观点、理由、例子、重申观点。
◆ OREO：意见、理由、例子、重申意见。
◆ 回答、理由、例子、信息。
◆ CREI：主张、推理、例子、影响。
◆ 连接、回答、推理、例子。

学生完成了四个例子的练习。前两个先写出答案，以熟悉结构与逻辑；随后练习不做准备直接回答，尝试在讲话时使用 PREP。

homework.en:
Complete the last two written examples, using the structures introduced in class to organize the answers.

If possible, also practise the short dialogue between the bank robber and the security guard.
homework.zh:
完成最后两个书面例子，运用课堂介绍的结构组织答案。

如果可以，也请练习银行劫匪与保安之间的简短对话。

students.name: Zoey
students.en:
✓ 𝑷𝒂𝒓𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒊𝒑𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Zoey presented first. She appeared a little tired while speaking with the group, but completed her turn.

➜ 𝑨𝒕𝒕𝒊𝒕𝒖𝒅𝒆 𝒕𝒐𝒘𝒂𝒓𝒅 𝒘𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈:
Zoey said she does not really like writing. This expresses her preference; it does not establish a difficulty with writing or a refusal to do the task.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒔𝒖𝒑𝒑𝒐𝒓𝒕:
She could begin by saying one idea aloud, then writing that idea as a short sentence to prepare for her speech.
students.zh:
✓【参与】：
Zoey 是第一位展示的学生。与大家讲话时，她看起来有些疲倦，但完成了自己的发言。

➜【对写作的态度】：
Zoey 说自己不太喜欢写作。这表达的是她的偏好，并不能证明她写作有困难，也不表示她拒绝完成任务。

➜【建议支持】：
她可以先口头说出一个想法，再把它写成一个简短句子，为演讲做准备。

students.name: Arthur
students.en:
✓ 𝑬𝒏𝒆𝒓𝒈𝒚 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒏𝒕𝒉𝒖𝒔𝒊𝒂𝒔𝒎:
Arthur has now presented. He brought good energy and enthusiasm to his delivery, giving his speech a lively feel.

➜ 𝑷𝒂𝒄𝒆 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒑𝒂𝒖𝒔𝒆𝒔:
He spoke a little quickly. A slower pace with more pauses would make his ideas easier to follow and give the audience time to absorb each point. The aim is to keep his enthusiasm while giving his words more space.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Practise one complete sentence at a time, then pause briefly before starting the next. Keep the same expressive energy while making sure every word is clear.

➜ 𝑾𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈:
Arthur took a little more time with the writing activity. This observation concerns his writing pace; the quality or completeness of his written work has not yet been described.
students.zh:
✓【能量与热情】：
Arthur 已经完成展示。他的表达有能量、有热情，让演讲显得生动。

➜【语速与停顿】：
他的语速稍快。放慢一些并增加停顿，会让听众更容易跟上，也有时间理解每个要点。目标是保留热情，同时给词句更多空间。

➜【建议练习】：
一次练习一个完整句子，之后稍作停顿再开始下一句。保持同样的表达能量，同时确保每个词都清楚。

➜【写作】：
Arthur 完成写作活动时需要稍多一些时间。这项观察涉及书写速度；目前还没有描述作品的质量或完成程度。

students.name: Merlin
students.en:
✓ 𝑾𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒊𝒏𝒈 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒏𝒈𝒂𝒈𝒆𝒎𝒆𝒏𝒕:
Merlin wrote very quickly and was already continuing with his writing before the class moved to the next activity. He appeared to enjoy the writing task and showed enthusiasm for getting his ideas onto paper.

✓ 𝑷𝒂𝒓𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒊𝒑𝒂𝒕𝒊𝒐𝒏:
Merlin has now completed his speaking turn.

➜ 𝑷𝒂𝒄𝒆:
He spoke a little quickly. Slowing down and pausing between complete ideas would give listeners more time to follow his message.

➜ 𝑬𝒙𝒑𝒓𝒆𝒔𝒔𝒊𝒐𝒏 𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝒆𝒏𝒆𝒓𝒈𝒚:
His delivery had little emotional expression or vocal variation, making it sound mechanical. He communicated the words, but the presentation felt more like ordinary conversation than a speech directed toward an audience. The next focus is adding purposeful emphasis and energy so listeners can hear which ideas matter.

➜ 𝑺𝒖𝒈𝒈𝒆𝒔𝒕𝒆𝒅 𝒑𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒕𝒊𝒄𝒆:
Choose one sentence, mark an important word, and practise saying it with expression that matches its meaning. Pause at the end before continuing, keeping that deliberate pace and energy through the next sentence.

Use his written work for rehearsal: mark an important word in each sentence, emphasize it with expression that matches the meaning, and pause before the next idea.
students.zh:
✓【写作与投入】：
Merlin 写得很快，在全班进入下一个活动之前，他已经继续写了不少内容。他似乎享受这项写作任务，积极地把想法写在纸上。

✓【参与】：
Merlin 已经完成了自己的发言。

➜【语速】：
他讲得稍快。放慢速度，并在完整想法之间停顿，可以给听众更多时间理解信息。

➜【表现力与能量】：
他的表达中情感和声音变化较少，听起来有些机械。他说出了内容，但更像普通交谈，而不是面向听众的演讲。下一步是加入有目的的重音和能量，让听众听出哪些想法最重要。

➜【建议练习】：
选择一句话，标出一个重要的词，用符合意思的情感说出来。句末停顿后再继续，把这种有意识的节奏和能量保持到下一句。

用自己的书面材料排练：为每句话标出一个重要词语，用符合意思的表现力突出它，再停顿进入下一个想法。

students.name: Charles
students.en:
✓ What worked: Charles gave a short but complete answer to the debate question. He communicated his response without leaving it unfinished.

→ Next focus: Develop his reasons a little further. Using “First... Second... Finally...”, he can add a brief explanation or example to help the audience understand why he holds his position.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: A useful practice pattern is “I think… because… For example…”. After giving the example, he can add one sentence explaining how it supports his answer. This helps listeners understand the reasoning rather than having to guess the connection. He can develop one reason at a time, keeping the complete ending he already achieved instead of trying to add several unrelated ideas.
students.zh:
✓ 今天的表现：Charles 对辩论问题给出了简短但完整的回答。他表达了自己的回应，没有半途停下。

→ 下一步：把理由展开一些。使用“First… Second… Finally…”时，可以在每点后补充一个简短解释或例子，让听众明白他为什么持有这个立场。

➜ 意义与练习方法：可以练习“I think… because… For example…”。说完例子后，再用一句话解释它如何支持答案，让听众理解推理，而不必自己猜测联系。他可以一次展开一个理由，保留已经做到的完整收尾，而不是一下加入几个不相关的想法。

students.name: Ethan
students.en:
• Classroom participation: Ethan had difficulty settling his laughter during another student’s speech, which interrupted the speaker’s turn. He also needed reminders about considerate use of shared classroom space.

→ Next focus: Practise listening quietly while others present and keeping feet on the floor. If laughter starts, he can pause, take a breath, and return his attention to the speaker. Gentle reinforcement at home will help him build these habits and give classmates a respectful opportunity to share their ideas.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: A simple listening routine can make the expectation concrete: face the speaker, keep feet still, and wait until the turn has finished before responding. Practising that routine during a short family speaking activity gives him a clear situation in which to try it. The purpose is to protect each speaker’s time and attention; it is a participation habit to develop, not a judgment about his character.
students.zh:
• 课堂参与：Ethan 在另一位同学演讲时不太容易平复笑声，打断了对方的发言。他也需要提醒，在使用共享课堂空间时顾及他人。

→ 下一步：练习在别人展示时安静倾听，并让双脚放在地面。如果开始发笑，可以先停一下、做一次呼吸，再把注意力回到讲述者身上。家长在家温和强化这些习惯，可以帮助他逐渐养成更有分寸的参与方式，给同学一个受到尊重、能够分享想法的机会。

➜ 意义与练习方法：可以把倾听要求变成具体步骤：面向发言者、双脚保持稳定、等对方讲完再回应。在家进行一个简短的轮流发言活动，可以给他练习这套步骤的明确情境。目标是尊重每位发言者的时间和注意力；这是需要培养的参与习惯，而不是对性格的评价。

students.name: James
students.en:
✓ What worked: James gave a detailed yet concise response. He shared his own thoughts, explained how he felt, and put effort into helping the audience understand his reasoning. His answer showed that giving more information does not have to mean speaking for longer.

→ Next focus: Keep this balance of a clear point and a focused explanation, using specific details that directly support his position.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: To check that balance, he can identify the sentence containing his main point and ask whether each detail helps explain it. A useful closing phrase is “This is why I think…”. It brings the explanation back to his position without repeating the whole answer. The goal is not to speak longer for its own sake, but to make each added detail meaningful to the audience.
students.zh:
✓ 今天的表现：James 的回答既有细节，也保持了简洁。他分享自己的想法、解释感受，并努力让听众理解他的理由。他的回答说明，信息更丰富并不一定意味着要讲得更久。

→ 下一步：继续保持“清楚的观点＋集中的解释”这一平衡，使用能够直接支持立场的具体细节。

➜ 意义与练习方法：为了检查这种平衡，他可以找出表达主要观点的句子，再看每个细节是否有助于解释它。结尾可以使用“This is why I think…”，把解释带回立场，而不用重复整个答案。目标不是为了延长时间而多说，而是让每个补充细节都对听众有意义。

students.name: Berlingo
students.en:
✓ What worked: Berlingo completed the task, organized his thoughts, and used “first,” “second,” and “finally.” He did not need to look at his paper.

→ Audience connection: He looked toward the screen earlier, so he should remember to turn back and address the people in front of him.

→ Delivery: Practise speaking slightly louder and slower, pausing between points to make his words clearer.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: He can choose a listener before beginning each point, say the complete idea, and pause before turning to another part of the audience. This combines eye contact with the structure he already remembers. A short recording can help him check whether the final words remain audible. The goal is to share a prepared idea with people, rather than direct the speech toward the screen.
students.zh:
✓ 今天的表现：Berlingo 完成了任务，组织了自己的想法，并使用“first”“second”“finally”。他不需要看稿纸。

→ 听众交流：前面讲话时，他看向了屏幕，因此要记得转回来，面向眼前的听众表达。

→ 表达练习：声音稍微大一点，语速稍微慢一点，在要点之间停顿，让每个词更容易听清。

➜ 意义与练习方法：他可以在每个要点开始前选定一位听众，看着对方把完整想法说完，停顿后再转向另一侧。这能把眼神交流与已经记住的结构结合起来。录一小段视频，也能帮助他检查最后几个词是否听得见。目标是向人分享准备好的想法，而不是对着屏幕讲话。

students.name: Yiyi
students.en:
✓ What worked: Yiyi approached the activity seriously and was able to give her answers.

→ Main focus: Make her reasoning easier to follow, particularly in the third point. Each reason should clearly support her position on the question.

→ Practice: Review the third point using reason → explanation → link to her position, checking that listeners can understand how it supports her argument.

➜ Why this matters and how to practise: She can test the third reason by asking “Does this explain why my side is stronger?” Then try “This supports my position because…”, using a simple example to make the connection visible. If the link is difficult to explain, she can revise the reason rather than add more unrelated detail. This helps her serious preparation become a line of reasoning the audience can follow.
students.zh:
✓ 今天的表现：Yiyi 认真对待活动，并能够说出自己的答案。

→ 主要方向：让理由更容易理解，尤其是第三点。每一个理由都应该清楚地支持她对问题的立场。

→ 练习建议：按照“理由→解释→联系自己的立场”检查第三点，确认听众能理解这个想法如何支撑她的论点。

➜ 意义与练习方法：她可以用“这一点是否解释了为什么我的立场更有力？”来检查第三个理由，再尝试“This supports my position because…”，用简单例子把联系说清楚。如果很难解释这种联系，可以修改理由，而不是加入更多不相关细节。这样能把认真准备转化成听众能够跟上的推理过程。

classContent.en:
1. Choosing a position and supporting it

Students discussed “If we are bad at doing something, should we still do it?” They chose a side and practised explaining their reasoning through:

“We should / shouldn’t, because... First... Second... Finally...”

The focus was on giving a clear argument with supporting explanations, while using purposeful hand gestures and speaking with conviction.

2. Personal connection: Technology in my life

Students practised answering “What is one piece of technology in your life?” They introduced their choice and organized their ideas using first, second, and finally.

The aim was to connect the topic to their own experiences, giving specific personal details that help the audience understand technology’s role in their lives.
classContent.zh:
1. 选择立场，并提供支持

学生讨论了“如果我们不擅长做一件事，还应该继续做吗？”他们选择一方，并用以下顺序练习解释理由：

“We should / shouldn’t, because… First… Second… Finally…”

重点是提出清楚的论点，并给出支撑性解释，同时配合有目的的手势，以有信念、有说服力的方式表达。

2. 个人连接：我生活中的科技

学生练习回答“What is one piece of technology in your life?”，介绍自己选择的一项科技，并用“first、second、finally”组织想法。

目标是把话题与自己的经历联系起来，加入具体的个人细节，帮助听众理解科技在自己生活中的作用。

homework.en:
Technology is a part of our lives

If possible, write out your own speech about one piece of technology that is important to you and how it affects your life. Students are encouraged to write the speech themselves.

Organize your speech around what, why and how: What is the technology? Why is it important to you? How does it affect you?

Finish with a message for the audience.

Prepare a speech lasting one to two minutes.
homework.zh:
科技是我们生活的一部分

如果可以，请写出自己的演讲稿，选择一种对你很重要的科技，并说明它如何影响你的生活。鼓励同学们尽量自己完成写作。

围绕“是什么、为什么、如何”来组织演讲：这是什么科技？它为什么对你重要？它如何影响你？

结尾要给听众留下一个想传达的信息。

演讲时长为一到两分钟。

students.name: Arthur
students.en:
✓ Warm-up

✓ What worked: Arthur presented an argument and supported it with evidence, giving his response a useful foundation.

→ Voice and clarity: His mask slightly muffled his voice. When speaking with a mask, he should aim for approximately 20% more volume while keeping his words clear.

→ Organization: Clear transitions would make his points easier to follow. Phrases such as “My first contention,” “My first argument,” or “My first point” help judges and the opposing side identify each argument, especially when debate delivery becomes faster.

→ Development: His response was somewhat short. He can expand the explanation of his evidence and show how it supports his argument. For the next attempt, practise a clear transition → argument → supporting evidence → explanation, maintaining an audible voice throughout.

Mini debate

Arthur supported his opening response with evidence, but his wording in the mini debate was sometimes difficult to understand. One term was unclear to the listener, making the intended point harder to identify. Clear articulation, sufficient volume while wearing his mask, and explicit transitions remain important.

He did attempt to rebut April. To make that response easier to follow, he should first state the point she made and then explain why he disagrees. Because both sides’ claims were not always clear, it became difficult to develop the exchange.

Practice: Use “My opponent argued… I disagree because… My evidence is…”, allowing enough time to explain each connection.
students.zh:
✓ 热身练习

✓ 表现亮点：Arthur 提出了论点，并用证据加以支持，为他的回答打下了良好的基础。

→ 声音与清晰度：口罩稍微影响了声音的传递。戴口罩发言时，可以尝试把音量提高约20%，同时保持吐字清楚。

→ 内容组织：更清晰的过渡表达能让他的要点更容易被听懂。例如“My first contention”“My first argument”或“My first point”，可以帮助评委和对方辨认每个论点，尤其是在辩论语速加快时。

→ 内容展开：他的回答稍短，可以进一步解释证据，并说明证据如何支持论点。下一次练习可以按照“清楚的过渡 → 论点 → 支持证据 → 解释”的顺序展开，并在整个过程中保持声音清楚可闻。

小型辩论

Arthur 在开场回答中用证据支持了论点，但在小型辩论中，有些措辞不容易听懂。有一个词听众没有听清，因此更难辨认他想表达的要点。清晰的吐字、戴口罩时足够的音量，以及明确的过渡表达，仍然很重要。

他确实尝试反驳 April。为了让回应更容易理解，他应先复述她提出的要点，再解释自己为什么不同意。由于双方的主张有时都不够清楚，交锋就难以进一步展开。

练习方法：使用“My opponent argued… I disagree because… My evidence is…”，给每一步之间的联系留出充分的解释时间。

students.name: Audrey
students.en:
✓ Warm-up

✓ What worked: Audrey began using more transitional words, making the sequence of her points clearer and showing progress in organizing her response.

→ Conviction: Her delivery could be firmer and more assertive. Clear, decisive statements and stronger emphasis on key words would help communicate confidence in her position while keeping disagreement respectful.

→ Evidence and detail: Her examples and evidence need clearer explanation. She can describe the example more specifically, explain what it demonstrates, and connect it directly to her argument. With no time limit for this exercise, she has room to develop her reasoning more fully.

→ Practice: Use transition → clear argument → specific example → explanation, pausing briefly before emphasizing the main conclusion. Her improved transitions provide a useful foundation for a stronger, more developed response.

Mini debate

Audrey showed clear progress in her use of debate terminology, structure, and logic. She summarized her opponents’ points well and became more responsive to what they had actually said, using the pattern “My opponent said… However…” Her examples also supported her arguments effectively.

At times, she hesitated or repeated words, making her delivery less smooth. She seemed to be managing several ideas at once. Her next focus is expressing one response clearly before introducing another, using short sentences and brief pauses. She can retain the stronger terminology while giving herself enough time to communicate the reasoning behind it.

Practice: Identify one opposing claim, pause, then deliver one rebuttal with a supporting example.
students.zh:
✓ 热身练习

✓ 表现亮点：Audrey 开始使用更多过渡词，让要点的先后顺序更加清楚，也体现了她在组织回答方面的进步。

→ 表达信念：她的表达可以更加坚定、有力。清楚、明确的陈述，以及对关键词更有力的强调，能让听众感受到她对自己立场的信心，同时保持有礼、有分寸的不同意见表达。

→ 证据与细节：例子和证据还需要解释得更清楚。她可以更具体地描述例子，说明它证明了什么，再直接联系到自己的论点。这次练习没有时间限制，因此她有空间把推理展开得更充分。

→ 练习方法：按照“过渡 → 明确的论点 → 具体例子 → 解释”来组织回答，在强调主要结论前稍作停顿。她在过渡表达上的进步，为更有力、更充分的回答打下了良好基础。

小型辩论

Audrey 在辩论术语、结构和逻辑的运用上取得了明显进步。她能够较好地概括对方的观点，也更能针对对方实际说过的内容作出回应，使用“My opponent said… However…”这样的表达。她的例子也有效地支持了论点。

有时她会犹豫或重复词语，使表达不够流畅。她似乎同时在处理几个想法。接下来应先用简短的句子和适当的停顿，把一个回应讲清楚，再引入下一个。她可以继续使用更准确的辩论术语，同时给自己足够的时间把背后的推理表达完整。

练习方法：找出对方的一个论点，停顿一下，再提出一个反驳，并配上支持性的例子。

students.name: Teresa
students.en:
✓ Warm-up

✓ What worked: She maintained good pacing, organized her response well, and provided plenty of examples to support her side.

→ Emphasis: Her main arguments would benefit from clearer, more decisive statements. Brief pauses between points—and after an important claim—would give listeners time to absorb the reasoning and recognize its significance.

→ Impact and comparison: After each example, she should explain why it matters: who is affected, what changes, and why that outcome strengthens her side’s case compared with the opposing position. This helps listeners understand not only the argument, but why they should support it.

→ Practice: Use clear claim → example → impact → comparison, finishing with a sentence explaining why her side should win the debate.

Mini debate

Teresa’s points in the mini debate needed clearer wording. Listeners should be able to identify exactly what she is arguing before hearing the supporting explanation. Her priority is to state one complete claim, explain it, and show how it supports her side. This will also give the opposing speaker a clear point to respond to.

Practice: Begin with “Our argument is…,” then add a reason and an example before moving on.
students.zh:
✓ 热身练习

✓ 表现亮点：她保持了良好的节奏，回答组织清晰，并提供了丰富的例子来支持自己的立场。

→ 强调重点：主要论点可以表达得更明确、更坚定。在要点之间，以及重要观点之后稍作停顿，能让听众有时间理解推理，并意识到它的重要性。

→ 影响与比较：每个例子之后，她都应解释它为什么重要：谁会受到影响，会发生什么变化，以及与对方立场相比，这一结果为什么更能支持己方。这能让听众不仅理解论点，也明白为什么应该支持她的立场。

→ 练习方法：按照“明确的主张 → 例子 → 影响 → 比较”展开，最后用一句话说明为什么己方应该赢得辩论。

小型辩论

Teresa 在小型辩论中的论点需要表达得更清楚。听众应该先能准确理解她主张什么，再听支持这一主张的解释。她的首要任务是说出一个完整的论点，解释它，并说明它如何支持己方立场。这样也能给对方一个明确的回应对象。

练习方法：先说“Our argument is…”，接着补充理由和例子，再进入下一个要点。

students.name: Ning
students.en:
✓ Warm-up

✓ Structure and conclusion: Ning organized her response clearly and included a conclusion, an important step in bringing her arguments together and giving the speech a definite ending.

✓ Specific details: She provided concrete details that helped listeners picture what she was describing. Her explanations were clear and well developed, making her reasoning easier to understand. Overall, this was a strong performance.

→ Next step: Build on this structure by using the conclusion to restate her position, bring together her strongest supporting points, and explain why the outcome matters. This will help the audience leave with a clear understanding of her case.

Mini debate

Ning’s earlier response had clear organization, specific details, and a conclusion. During the debate, however, she relied more on her prepared points than on responding directly to Audrey’s preceding speech. The next step is to connect her strong content to the live exchange: listen for the opponent’s exact claim, identify the disagreement, and explain why her response challenges it.

Practice: Note one key claim while listening, then begin with “Audrey argued that… Our response is…” before adding her own evidence and explaining the impact.
students.zh:
✓ 热身练习

✓ 结构与结论：Ning 的回答条理清楚，并加入了结论。这是把论点整合起来、让演讲有明确收尾的重要一步。

✓ 具体细节：她提供了具体细节，帮助听众在脑海中呈现她所描述的内容。她的解释清楚、展开充分，让推理更容易被理解。整体而言，这是一次很好的表现。

→ 下一步：在现有结构的基础上，用结论重申自己的立场，归纳最有力的支撑要点，并说明结果为什么重要。这样能让听众在演讲结束时清楚理解她的论证。

小型辩论

Ning 前面的回答组织清晰，有具体细节，也有结论。但在辩论中，她更多依赖准备好的要点，没有直接回应 Audrey 紧接着在她之前所作的发言。下一步是把她扎实的内容与现场交锋联系起来：听清对方的具体主张，找出分歧，并解释自己的回应为什么能挑战这一主张。

练习方法：倾听时记下一个关键论点，先说“Audrey argued that… Our response is…”，再补充自己的证据，并解释其影响。

students.name: April
students.en:
✓ Warm-up

✓ Applying feedback: April incorporated the guidance given during earlier speaking turns. Her response had a clear structure, well-developed content, and supporting examples, showing that she listened to the feedback and applied it to her own presentation.

→ Articulation and clarity: Some words blended together, making parts of her speech less distinct. This could become more noticeable at faster debate speeds, when judges and the opposing side need to follow her reasoning closely.

→ Practice: Rehearse one argument at a slightly slower pace, finishing each word clearly and pausing between ideas. Once the wording is consistently clear, gradually increase speed while maintaining that precision. Her content and organization provide a strong foundation; clearer articulation will help listeners follow the full argument.

Mini debate

April’s earlier speech showed good structure, supporting examples, and an ability to apply feedback. In the mini debate, her next priority was defining her main points more clearly. Each claim should establish a specific issue that both speakers can examine and respond to. This would help the exchange move beyond opposing statements toward a clear comparison of arguments.

Her articulation remains another useful focus: finishing words distinctly and pausing between ideas will help listeners identify those points, particularly at faster speeds.

Practice: State one concise claim, explain why it matters, and support it with an example before moving to the next issue.
students.zh:
✓ 热身练习

✓ 运用反馈：April 把前面几轮发言中给出的指导运用到了自己的展示里。她的回答结构清楚、内容展开充分，并有例子支持，体现了她认真听取反馈并在自己的表达中加以实践。

→ 吐字与清晰度：有些词连在了一起，让部分表达不够清晰。在辩论语速更快时，这个问题可能更加明显，而评委和对方都需要准确跟上她的推理。

→ 练习方法：先用稍慢的速度练习一个论点，把每个词说完整、说清楚，并在想法之间留出停顿。等到每次都能清楚表达后，再逐步加快语速，同时保持这种准确度。她的内容和组织已经有良好基础；更清楚的吐字能帮助听众理解完整的论证。

小型辩论

April 前面的发言结构良好，有支持性的例子，也能应用反馈。在小型辩论中，她下一步的重点是把主要论点界定得更清楚。每个主张都应提出一个具体问题，让双方都能围绕它分析和回应。这样能帮助交锋从各说各的立场，发展成对论点的清晰比较。

吐字仍然是一个值得关注的方向：清楚地说完每个词，并在想法之间停顿，能帮助听众辨认要点，尤其是在语速较快时。

练习方法：先说出一个简洁的主张，解释它为什么重要，再用例子支持它，然后进入下一个问题。

classContent.en:
Students began with a debate warm-up discussing whether AI-generated pictures could be considered “normal.” They practised stating a position, supporting it with evidence and examples, and organizing their responses so listeners could follow each argument. Feedback was shared between turns, giving students opportunities to apply the guidance they heard.

The main speaking and reasoning skills were:

◆ Clear transitions: Introduce arguments with phrases such as “My first contention,” “My first argument,” or “My first point.” These signposts help judges and the opposing side follow the case, especially at faster debate speeds.
◆ Evidence and explanation: Give specific examples, explain what they demonstrate, and connect them to the argument. With no time limit for this exercise, students were encouraged to develop their reasoning fully.
◆ Impact and comparison: Explain who is affected, why the outcome matters, and why their side’s position produces a stronger outcome than the alternative.
◆ Conviction and delivery: Use firm, respectful statements, purposeful emphasis, clear articulation, and pauses that allow important points to register.
◆ Conclusions: Bring the arguments together and finish with a clear statement of the position and its significance.

Students then took part in mini debates: April versus Arthur, followed by Audrey versus Teresa and Ning. This gave them an opportunity to apply the earlier speaking guidance in an opposing-side format.

We also explored “Students should be able to grade their own teachers.” The discussion considered the perspectives of students, parents, teachers, principals, and education boards. Potential benefits included useful feedback for improvement, students raising concerns about safety, and better support for students. Possible concerns included retaliatory or false feedback, popularity and voting dynamics, differing perspectives, discrimination, and judging teachers before having sufficient information. These ideas provided a basis for considering competing interests and comparing the consequences of each side’s arguments.

The mini debates highlighted a shared priority: state a clear claim, identify the opponent’s claim accurately, and explain the disagreement. When both sides’ points remain unclear, the exchange becomes harder to follow and can turn into repeated assertions rather than a developing argument.
classContent.zh:
学生首先进行了辩论热身，讨论 AI 生成的图片能否被视为“正常”。他们练习表明立场，用证据和例子支持观点，并组织回答，让听众能够跟上每一个论点。发言之间分享了反馈，让学生有机会应用刚刚听到的指导。

主要练习的表达与推理能力包括：

◆ 清晰的过渡：用“My first contention”“My first argument”或“My first point”等表达引出论点。这些提示能帮助评委和对方理解论证，尤其是在辩论语速较快时。
◆ 证据与解释：提供具体例子，解释例子说明了什么，并将它与论点联系起来。这次练习没有时间限制，因此鼓励学生充分展开推理。
◆ 影响与比较：解释谁会受到影响，结果为什么重要，以及为什么己方立场带来的结果优于另一种选择。
◆ 信念与表达：使用坚定而尊重对方的陈述、有目的的重音、清晰的吐字，以及让重要观点被听懂的停顿。
◆ 结论：整合论点，以明确的立场及其意义结束发言。

随后，学生进行了小型辩论：April 对 Arthur，然后是 Audrey 对 Teresa 和 Ning。这让他们有机会在双方交锋的形式中应用前面的表达指导。

我们还探讨了“学生应该能够给自己的老师评分”。讨论考虑了学生、家长、教师、校长和教育主管部门的视角。可能的好处包括为改进提供有用反馈、让学生提出安全方面的顾虑，以及更好地支持学生。可能的问题包括报复性或不实反馈、受欢迎程度与投票的影响、不同视角、歧视，以及在信息不足时就评价教师。这些想法为分析不同利益诉求、比较双方论点带来的后果提供了基础。

小型辩论凸显了一个共同重点：提出清晰的主张，准确辨认对方的主张，并解释分歧。当双方的要点都不清楚时，交锋就更难跟上，也容易变成重复表态，而不是逐步推进的论证。

开篇立论：学生应该被允许给自己的老师评分

有条件的作业安排：Heidi 可能会布置作业。如果她没有布置，请完成以下任务。

建议分组：Arthur 和 Audrey 为正方；Teresa、Ning 和 April 为反方。

每位同学都应介绍辩题、解释关键概念，并提出三个支持己方立场的论点。

classContent.en:
We began with an impromptu warm-up: “If we are bad at doing something, should we still do it?” Students chose a position and developed three reasons using “We should / shouldn’t, because… First… Second… Finally…” The focus was on forming their own ideas and supporting each point with an explanation or example.

We then explored the WCA competition topic: “Students should not be allowed to be on social media.” We discussed different arguments and viewed social-media examples to make the issues more concrete. Students considered the perspectives of students, parents, teachers, and social-media companies.

Arguments supporting restrictions included reduced sleep, copying dangerous activities, cheating, anxiety from comparison, unsafe online contact, inappropriate content, pressure to seek attention, and addictive use. Arguments against restrictions included opportunities to learn, access current information, maintain friendships, share experiences, find inspiration, connect with different communities, and support others.

After this discussion, each student spoke for approximately one minute and 30 seconds, presenting arguments, supporting points, and examples. Their responses became more thorough, and they approached the task more seriously. This was an initial exercise in developing independent arguments and entering a debate mindset; we have not yet covered detailed competition structures or techniques.
classContent.zh:
我们先进行了即兴演讲热身，讨论“如果我们不擅长做某件事，还应该继续做吗？”学生选择一个立场，并使用“We should / shouldn’t, because… First… Second… Finally…”的结构展开三个理由。重点是形成自己的想法，并用解释或例子支持每一个要点。

随后，我们探讨了WCA比赛题目：“学生不应该被允许使用社交媒体。”我们讨论了不同的论点，并通过社交媒体的例子让这些问题更加具体。学生思考了学生、家长、老师以及社交媒体公司的不同角度。

支持限制使用社交媒体的论点包括睡眠减少、模仿危险活动、作弊、因比较而产生焦虑、不安全的网络接触、不适当的内容、寻求关注的压力，以及成瘾性使用。反对限制的论点包括学习机会、获取最新信息、维持友谊、分享经历、获得灵感、与不同社群建立联系，以及支持他人。

讨论之后，每位学生进行了大约1分30秒的发言，陈述论点、支撑要点和例子。他们的回答变得更加充分，也更加认真地完成了任务。这是一次发展独立论证能力、进入辩论思维状态的初步练习；我们还没有学习具体的比赛结构或技巧。
